evidence: Hashes: frozen task/environment/Dockerfile 0a75419e..., seed_data.json a1c65c80..., hireops_rules.md 38fff76c..., integration.md 1b56dd3f..., instruction.md 256c5b5d..., workbook 6d44970b..., SKILL.md 8f2b660d..., quality-checks.md 2e1ec096... all equal the values in qc/runs/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r8/manifest.json inputs. (1) /app empty except .gitkeep: task/environment/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template Dockerfile (cmp; both sha256 0a75419e...). Lines 14-23: 'COPY instructions/ /instructions/', 'COPY assets/ /assets/', then 'mkdir -p /app && git -C /app init ... touch /app/.gitkeep && git -C /app add .gitkeep && git -C /app commit'. No COPY of solution/ or tests/; the only build context is environment/, which contains exactly Dockerfile, assets/seed_data.json, instructions/hireops_rules.md, instructions/integration.md (ls -la). Global npm installs are only express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 (lines 9-12), plain runtime libraries, no starter. (2) No starter/skeleton/schema/route list/partial UI: hireops_rules.md:3-5 says 'Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages are yours'; integration.md:14 'How routes and files are laid out under /app is up to you.' The rules give behavioural rules and HTTP status semantics (401/403/404/409, rules.md:21-23, 78) which are the public spec, not an implementation; no SQL schema, no endpoint list, no HTML/JS. integration.md differs from the template only by the added delivery/symlink paragraph (lines 16-19), which is runtime policy, not answer content. (3) Seed asset is input data only: top-level keys generated_note, stages, candidate_status_labels, thread_page_size, users, jobs, applications(id, job_id, candidate_name, candidate_email, source, stage, position, reject_reason, rejected_from), messages(application_id, sender_id, body, created_at), notes, reads(user_id, application_id, read_count). No expected outputs, precomputed unread counts, seen flags, activity lines, or grader values; searching for expected/criterion/rubric/judge/score/golden/solution/probe found none (only message bodies 'I have passed your notes...' and a note 'answers'). It is byte-identical to solution/app/src/seed_data.json, which is the supplied input the golden copies, not a deliverable. The functional prompt's Z protocol checks seeded figures (Lena unread 1, Platform Engineer order, Noor's note) that the agent must correctly load and derive from read_count; providing the raw inputs for these is the intended 'inputs', not a leak of the derived result. (4) /instructions does not reproduce criterion text or the rubric: grep of environment/ and instruction.md for judge|rubric|criteri|dimension|reward|weight|score.py|playwright|claude|glm|/tests|sentinel|probe|golden|solution|hro_|GATE returned no matches. A token shingle comparison of both /instructions files against every tests/**/judge.toml, prompt.md and app_context.md found zero 12-word overlaps and only four 8-word overlaps, all in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml restating public behaviour rules ('the reason is shown and keyboard focus', 'arrive at the bottom of that stage in board order'), i.e. criteria grading the public spec, not the spec leaking criterion wording. Counterexample attempts: a broken app that could pass because of a leak would need a copyable implementation or precomputed answers in the agent image; none exists, so an agent must build server, storage, live updates, undo and permission logic itself. A conforming alternative that could fail because of this row: none, since the environment imposes no route/schema/layout. This row is static image-content review; the Dockerfile and context fully determine image contents beyond the pinned node:22-bookworm-slim base, so no runtime build evidence is required for it. No Docker build was run in this review.
